get.summary:
Lists spaces that are direct children of the specified organization
resource. `list()` provides a strongly consistent view of the
spaces underneath the specified parent resource. `list()` returns
spaces sorted based upon the (ascending) lexical ordering of their
`display_name`. The caller must have `resourcemanager.spaces.list`
permission on the identified parent.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description:
Optional. A pagination token returned from a previous call to
[ListSpaces] [pivox.api.v1.Spaces.ListSpaces] that
indicates from where listing should continue.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Optional. The maximum number of spaces to return in the response.
The server can return fewer spaces than requested.
If unspecified, server picks an appropriate default.

parameters.name: showDeleted
parameters.description:
Optional. Indicate that spaces in the `DELETE_REQUESTED` state should
also be returned. Normally only `ACTIVE` spaces are returned.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional. An expression for filtering the results of the request.
Filter rules are case insensitive. Some eligible fields for filtering are:

+ `displayName`
+ `state`
+ `labels` (supports key and key=value matching)
+ `createTime` (supports comparison operators)

Some examples of filter strings:

+ `displayName = "My Space"` - returns spaces with display name
  "My Space".
+ `displayName = "My*"` - returns spaces whose display name starts
  with "My".
+ `state = ACTIVE` - returns only active spaces.
+ `labels.color:*` - returns spaces that have the label "color".
+ `labels.color = red` - returns spaces where label "color" is "red".
+ `createTime > "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"` - returns spaces created
  after the given timestamp.

For more information, see [AIP-160](https://aip.dev/160).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. The default
order is ascending. Use "desc" after a field name for descending.
Supported fields:

+ `displayName`
+ `createTime`
+ `name`

Example: `createTime desc, displayName`

If not specified, the results are ordered by `name` ascending.

get.summary:
Retrieves the space identified by the specified `name` (for example,
`organizations/123/spaces/my-space`).
get.description:
The caller must have `resourcemanager.spaces.get` permission
for this space.

delete.summary:
Marks the space identified by the specified
`name` (for example, `organizations/123/spaces/my-space`) for deletion.
delete.description:
This method will only affect the space if it has a lifecycle state of
[ACTIVE][pivox.api.v1.Space.State.ACTIVE].

This method changes the Space's lifecycle state from
[ACTIVE][pivox.api.v1.Space.State.ACTIVE]
to
[DELETE_REQUESTED][pivox.api.v1.Space.State.DELETE_REQUESTED].
The deletion starts at an unspecified time,
at which point the Space is no longer accessible.

Until the deletion completes, you can check the lifecycle state
checked by retrieving the space with [GetSpace]
[pivox.api.v1.Spaces.GetSpace],
and the space remains visible to [ListSpaces]
[pivox.api.v1.Spaces.ListSpaces].
However, you cannot update the space.

After the deletion completes, the space is not retrievable by
the [GetSpace]
[pivox.api.v1.Spaces.GetSpace] and
[ListSpaces]
[pivox.api.v1.Spaces.ListSpaces] method.

This method behaves idempotently, such that deleting a `DELETE_REQUESTED`
space will not cause an error, but also won't do anything.

If `force=true`, the 30-day grace window is skipped: the LRO
synchronously cascades all child data and frees the slug. The
space is unrecoverable.

The caller must have `resourcemanager.spaces.delete` permissions for this
space.

parameters.name: etag
parameters.description:
Optional. The etag known to the client for the expected state of the space.
This is to be used for optimistic concurrency.

parameters.name: validateOnly
parameters.description:
Optional. If set to true, the request will only validate the request
without persisting it.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Optional. If true, bypasses the 30-day grace window: the LRO
synchronously cascades all child data (assets, requests, line
items, space-scope member bindings, …) and frees the space slug.
The space is unrecoverable. Defaults to false (soft-delete with
grace; recoverable via `UndeleteSpace` until purge_time).

patch.summary:
Updates the `display_name` and labels of the space identified by the
specified `name` (for example, `organizations/123/spaces/my-space`).
Deleting all labels requires an update mask for labels field.
patch.description:
The caller must have `resourcemanager.spaces.update` permission for this
space.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Required. The new definition of the space.

displayName.description:
Optional. A user-assigned display name of the space.
When present it must be between 4 to 30 characters.
Allowed characters are: lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers,
hyphen, single-quote, double-quote, space, and exclamation point.

Example: `My Space`

createdBy.description: Output only. The identity that created this space.

updatedBy.description: Output only. The identity that last modified this space.

updateTime.description: Output only. The most recent time this resource was modified.

deletedBy.description: Output only. The identity that requested deletion of this space.

deleteTime.description: Output only. The time at which this resource was requested for deletion.

purgeTime.description:
Output only. The time at which this space will be purged.
Approximately 30 days after deletion.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the current value
of the Space resource. This may be sent on update and delete requests to
ensure the client has an up-to-date value before proceeding.

labels.description:
Optional. The labels associated with this space.

Label keys must be between 1 and 63 characters long and must conform
to the following regular expression: \[a-z\](\[-a-z0-9\]*\[a-z0-9\])?.

Label values must be between 0 and 63 characters long and must conform
to the regular expression (\[a-z\](\[-a-z0-9\]*\[a-z0-9\])?)?.

No more than 64 labels can be associated with a given resource.

Clients should store labels in a representation such as JSON that does not
depend on specific characters being disallowed.

Example: `"myBusinessDimension" : "businessValue"`

In this situation, update_mask is ignored.

get.summary:
Lists space-scope Members. Direct bindings only — does not include
members inherited from the parent org.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Optional. Maximum number of members to return.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: Optional. Page token from a previous ListMembers call.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional. An expression for filtering the results of the request.
Filterable fields:

+ `role` — exact match on a role resource name.
+ `principal_kind` — `user` or `group`.

For more information, see [AIP-160](https://aip.dev/160).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. Supported
fields: `createTime`, `role`. Default: `createTime` ascending.

post.summary:
Creates a space-scope Member binding. The principal must already
be a member of the parent organization. No ≥1-owner boundary at
space scope.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description:
Required. The Member to create. The `principal` oneof must be set
and `role` must reference an existing system role.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description:
Optional. A client-specified member ID. If provided, must be
`user-{user_id}` or `group-{group_id}` and must agree with the
`principal` oneof. If omitted, the server derives it from
`member.principal`.

get.summary:
Gets a space-scope Member by resource name. Members here are
only direct space-level bindings; users with implicit access via
their organization role do not appear as space Members.

parameters.name: etag
parameters.description: Optional. The etag known to the client for optimistic concurrency.

patch.summary: Updates a space-scope Member's role. Only `role` is mutable.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description:
A Member binds a principal (user or group) to a role at a scope
(organization or space). The single source of truth for "who has
what role where."

Required. The Member with updated fields. The `name` field must
identify the existing member.

role.description:
Required. Reference to the role this principal holds at this scope.
Format: `organizations/{organization}/roles/{role}`. v1 accepts only
system roles (`owner`, `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`).

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when this binding was created.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when this binding was last modified.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the current
value of the Member resource. Sent on update and delete requests for
optimistic concurrency control.

schema.description:
Required. The Member with updated fields. The `name` field must
identify the existing member.

A Member binds a principal (user or group) to a role at a scope

post.summary:
Returns the subset of requested permissions the caller is allowed
on the space. Resolution unions direct space-level bindings with
parent-org-level bindings — an org-admin is implicitly a
space-admin without an explicit space-scope Member row.

You can only use this method for a space that has a lifecycle state of
[DELETE_REQUESTED]
[Spaces.State.DELETE_REQUESTED].
After deletion starts, the space cannot be restored.

The request sent to the [UndeleteSpace]

name.description:
The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that
originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the
`name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

metadata.description:
Service-specific metadata associated with the operation.  It typically
contains progress information and common metadata such as create time.
Some services might not provide such metadata.  Any method that returns a
long-running operation should document the metadata type, if any.

done.description:
If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress.
If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is
available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

response.description:
The normal, successful response of the operation.  If the original
method returns no data on success, such as `Delete`, the response is
`google.protobuf.Empty`.  If the original method is standard
`Get`/`Create`/`Update`, the response should be the resource.  For other
methods, the response should have the type `XxxResponse`, where `Xxx`
is the original method name.  For example, if the original method name
is `TakeSnapshot()`, the inferred response type is
`TakeSnapshotResponse`.

longrunningOperation.description:
This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a
network API call.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

code.description:
The status code, which should be an enum value of
[google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description:
A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any
user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the
[google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized
by the client.

details.description:
A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of
message types for APIs to use.

rpcStatus.description:
The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for
different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
[API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

id.description:
The identity's stable UUID (firebase_identities.id). Always
populated when the column is non-null in the database, even for
soft-deleted identities.

displayName.description: Resolved display name. Empty for soft-deleted identities.

email.description: Resolved email address. Empty for soft-deleted identities.

isDeleted.description:
True when the identity has been soft-deleted. PII fields are
blanked out in that case while id is preserved.

typesActor.description:
Actor is a resolved reference to an identity. It is used flat on
resources to expose audit fields (created_by, updated_by, deleted_by)
per AIP-148, and can be reused at non-audit positions like assignee
or approver.

Actor lives in `pivox.types` (unversioned — type definitions are
shared infrastructure, not an API surface) so every domain package
(pivox.api.v1, pivox.ai.v1, pivox.assets.v1, pivox.iam.v1,
pivox.storage.v1) can reference it without crossing into a peer
domain — the api-linter's foreign-type-reference rule (AIP-215)
considers `pivox.types` a shared types namespace.

Resolution is performed server-side via the audit.Resolver, which
batches lookups against firebase_identities and caches recent
results. When the underlying identity is soft-deleted the resolver
blanks out PII (display_name, email) and sets is_deleted=true while
preserving the id so that historical references remain stable.

nextPageToken.description: Token for the next page of results.

spaces.description: The list of Spaces under the parent. This list can be paginated.

nextPageToken.description:
Pagination token.

If the result set is too large to fit in a single response, this token
is returned. It encodes the position of the current result cursor.
Feeding this value into a new list request with the `page_token` parameter
gives the next page of the results.

When `next_page_token` is not filled in, there is no next page and
the list returned is the last page in the result set.

Pagination tokens have a limited lifetime.

v1ListSpacesResponse.description:
A page of the response received from the
[ListSpaces][pivox.api.v1.Spaces.ListSpaces]
method.

A paginated response where more pages are available has
`next_page_token` set. This token can be used in a subsequent request to
retrieve the next request page.

NOTE: A response may contain fewer elements than the request `page_size` and
still have a `next_page_token`.

name.description:
The resource name of the member.
Format: `organizations/{organization}/members/{member}` or
        `organizations/{organization}/spaces/{space}/members/{member}`
where `{member}` is `user-{user_id}` or `group-{group_id}`.

role.description:
Required. Reference to the role this principal holds at this scope.
Format: `organizations/{organization}/roles/{role}`. v1 accepts only
system roles (`owner`, `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`).

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when this binding was created.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when this binding was last modified.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the current
value of the Member resource. Sent on update and delete requests for

v1Member.description:
Multi-parent: a Member lives under either an organization or a space.
The URL segment `{member}` encodes the principal as `user-{user_id}`
or `group-{group_id}` — uniqueness by construction means a given
principal can hold at most one role per scope.

Permission resolution unions org-level and space-level Member
bindings: an org owner is implicitly a space owner. Server-side
resolver is the source of truth; this proto defines only the wire
shape.
v1Member.title:
A Member binds a principal (user or group) to a role at a scope
(organization or space). The single source of truth for "who has
what role where."

v1Space.description:
A space is a high-level Pivox entity. It is a
container for ACLs, APIs, and other Pivox resources.

v1SpaceState.description:
Space lifecycle states.

 - STATE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified state.  This is only used/useful for distinguishing
unset values.
 - ACTIVE: The normal and active state.
 - DELETE_REQUESTED: The space has been marked for deletion by the user
(by invoking
[DeleteSpace][pivox.api.v1.Spaces.DeleteSpace])
or by the system (Pivox).
This can generally be reversed by invoking [UndeleteSpace]
[pivox.api.v1.Spaces.UndeleteSpace].

permissions.description:
Required. The permissions to check. Each entry is a permission ID
(e.g. `spaces.create`, `assets.assets.list`). Wildcards are not
supported.

v1SpacesTestIamPermissionsBody.description:
Request message for `Iam.TestIamPermissions`.

Used by clients (notably UI layers) to ask the server: "out of this
list of permissions, which ones does the caller actually have on
this resource?" The server resolves the caller's effective role at
the resource and returns the subset of requested permissions that
role grants.

permissions.description:
The subset of `TestIamPermissionsRequest.permissions` that the
caller is allowed on the resource. Permissions not in this list
are denied (or unknown).
